segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Karen. I saw your note about adding the field ops team. I pulled up the quote in the CRM, and right now you’re at 42 seats on the annual plan through March 31.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That’s right. We need to add 18 more, but only 12 of those people need admin access. The other 6 are read-only for reports.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. So 54 full seats total, 6 read-only. The pricing sheet has read-only at $18 per user per month and full seats at $74. Since you’re mid-term, billing would prorate from September 1 through March 31.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Can you send that as a separate invoice? Finance asked not to reopen the original PO if we can avoid it.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, that’s doable. I’ll mark it as a net-new add-on order tied to the existing contract. Invoice would be $7,672 before tax, due net 30. I’ll double-check the math with deal desk before I send it.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. And we still need the September 9 go-live for those users. Is that realistic if we sign this week?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes. If we have signature by Thursday, August 22, our implementation team can load the users on September 3, run the permissions review on the 5th, and you’d be ready for the 9th.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Sounds good. One thing, our legal team asked whether the add-on changes the renewal date.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: No, it stays co-termed to March 31, 2026. The order form will say no change to the master terms and no auto-renewal change.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Send the revised quote to me and copy James in finance. I’ll route it for signature once he confirms the PO number.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I’ll send it by end of day with the seat breakdown, prorated amount, and the September 1 service start date.
